question.text: Most of the hijackers were from this country, and one of their stated goals was for the United States to remove troops from this country.
question.answerHtml: Kingdom of Saudi Arabia [or al-Mamlakah al-Arabiyah as-Suudiyah]
question.clue: In October 2011, Nayif was announced as the successor to this country's leader, who accused Iran of hiring Mexican drug lords to assassinate its US ambassador.

swap.leadin: The Rashidun caliphate spread Islam throughout much of the Middle East.
swap.text: The caliphate was mostly composed of tribes of this ethnic group. Egypt, Iraq, and Algeria have large populations of this ethnic group, for which the peninsula containing Oman and Yemen is also named.
swap.clue: An emperor of this ethnicityheld theSecular Games on the thousandth anniversary of Rome's founding but was overthrown and killed by Decius ("DEE-shuss").

question.leadin: The secret Protocol of Sevres was a plan for Great Britain and France to "mediate" this event, in which they would take over the waterway in question.
question.text: Name this 1956 conflict in which Israel invaded Egypt in response to Gamal Abdel Nasser's nationalization of the namesake canal near the Sinai Peninsula.
question.clue: Robert Menzies failed to end this event peacefully, leading to the bombing of troops under Abdel Hakim Amer in this event's Operation Musketeer.

swap.leadin: Name the following Middle Eastern countries.
swap.text: This country's city of Madaba is known for its Byzantine map depicting the Holy Land. The city of Aqaba is also in this "Hashemite Kingdom."
swap.clue: Leila Khaled and the Sandinista Patrick Arguello were captured while trying to hijack a plane and take it to the Dawson's Field landing strip in this country which formed the Arab Federation with a western neighbour.

question.text: The Tang's western expansion was halted at the Battle of Talas, where they were defeated by this empire. This empire's capital of Baghdad, which contained the House of Wisdom, was destroyed by the Mongols in 1258.
question.clue: This dynasty rose to prominence after its army defeated Marwan II at the Battle of the Zab, and it saw advancements in algebra by al-Khwarizmi and optics by Ibn al-Haytham.

swap.leadin: Yazid I of this polity attacked Ali's family at the Battle of Karbala, and it fell after Marwan II's defeat at the Great Zab River.
swap.text: What polity, founded by Muawiyah I, governed Islam's conquest from North Africa to Mesopotamia and was the first Caliphate?
swap.clue: This empire rose to power after their victory in a conflict sparked by the killing of Uthman ibn Affan.

question.leadin: Mohammed Abdel Latif fired eight shots at this leader during a speech in Alexandria, but all eight missed.
question.text: Identify this leader whose one-party system was called the Liberation Rally. He joined with Muhammad Naguib to form the Free Officers Movement and overthrow Farouk I, and established the United Arab Republic.
question.clue: This leader helped overthrow King Farouk I in 1952 before founding the United Arab Republic in 1958.

swap.leadin: The prospect of peace with this country was denied by the signatories of the Khartoum Resolution, which outlined the "Three Nos."
swap.text: Name this Jewish state which controls disputed areas like Golan Heights and the West Bank.
swap.clue: This country's early "Austerity" period led it to sign a reparations agreement with West Germany under its first leader David Ben-Gurion.

question.text: Known on both sides for the holidays on which it started, this 1973 attack by Egypt and Syria led to the OPEC embargo.
question.answerHtml: Yom Kippur War [or Ramadan War; prompt on October War]
question.clue: Following this conflict Henry Kissinger successfully negotiated troop disengagements through his "shuttle diplomacy," and the United States' support of one side in this war led to an embargo by OPEC.

swap.leadin: Name these lands won by Israel in the 1967 Arab-Israeli war.
swap.text: Syria surrendered this area which also borders Jordan and Lebanon.
swap.clue: This territory lies within a buffer region demarcated by the "Purple Line" and is just east of the "Green Line" which extends around the edge of Lake Tiberias.

question.leadin: This battle is commemorated by the holiday of Ashura, which is celebrated during the month of Muharram.
question.text: Name this 680 AD battle in which a small force led by Muhammad's grandson Husayn was wiped out in Iraq. It triggered the Second Fitna, or Islamic civil war.
question.clue: Prior to this battle, the governor of Al-Basrah was sent by Yazid I to warn tribal leaders of reprisal if they fail to keep order among their people.

swap.text: Neither Lawrence nor Bell were involved in the Anglo-French negotiations of this 1916 treaty, which established zones of influence in former Ottoman territory in the Middle East.
swap.clue: Winston Churchill's White Paper was needed to clarify seemingly contradictory terms in it, as well as other secret promises and agreements reached at St. Jean de Maurienne, San Remo, and Sevres.

question.text: Mevlevlis considering whirling a form of this type of "remembrance" by which one gets closer to God and is able to feel God's presence.
question.clue: One of the main ways that Sufis demonstrate their devotion is through this rhythmic repetition of the name of Allah.

swap.text: Ataturk was the principle founder of this center-left political party, which dominated Turkish politics from 1923 to 1946. It is known primarily for its Six Arrows, including republicanism, secularism, nationalism, populism, statism, and revolutionism.

question.leadin: This man fought the Ridda Wars to combat apostasy, during which he was ably served by Khalid ibn al-Walid.
question.text: Name this man, who, after Mohammed's death, became the first Caliph, starting the Rashidun Caliphate and the process of Islamic expansion.
question.clue: Lubaina, Zinnira, and Bilal were among the many slaves this man used his wealth to emancipate , and the rest of his money went to fund an expedition at Tabuk.

swap.leadin: After cooperating in this battle to defeat the forces of Kitbuqa, Baibars assassinated Qutuz to become sultan.
swap.text: Name this 1260 battle in which Mamluk forces defeated a seemingly unstoppable force from the east that was headed toward Cairo.
swap.clue: The forces of Qutuz ] were inspired by the (+) rallying cry "Oh, my Islam" at this battle, during which a sultan of the Bahri dynasty led a feigned retreat.

question.leadin: The organization headed by this man was responsible for the assassination of ambassador Shlomo Argov in London, leading to the 1982 invasion of Lebanon.
question.text: Identify this namesake of a splinter group that rejected the 10 point program of the Palestine Liberation Organization. His nom de guerre translates to "father of the struggle."

swap.text: Both Jackie Kennedy's second husband Aristotle Onassis and his rival Stavros Niarchos benefited massively from the crisis surrounding the closure of this Middle Eastern waterway through which most of Europe's oil passed.
swap.clue: An American threat to devalue the pound ended Operation Musketeer, which began with a secretly planned Israeli invasion in concert with Britain and France to reconquer this place.

question.leadin: In 1899, the Spanish filibuster Luis Galvez declared this territory an independent republic with himself as president.
question.text: Name this territory that Brazil annexed from Bolivia in 1903.
question.clue: The Knights Hospitallers relocated to Cyprus after the fall of this city in 1291.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the assassinations of some 20th Century Middle Eastern leaders, FTPE.
swap.text: The son of the Kataeb Party's founder, this man organized and commanded the Lebanese Forces to combat Syrian occupation. Elected as Lebanon's president in 1982, he was killed in a bomb blast before he could take office, and his brother Amine was elected as his replacement.
swap.clue: This leader of the Phalangist Party, who united the Maronite militias of Lebanon. His party emerged victorious from the 1982 Lebanon War with Israeli support and the expulsion of the PLO.
